G.short_description: Procedural geomorphology derived from accepted G7 semantic fields and G3/G5/G6 surface, feature and hydrology truth.
G.purpose: Add deterministic valley, river-channel, bank, floodplain and erosion/deposition shaping without taking ownership of persistent Matter mutations, world identity, authority, persistence or material ontology.
G.expected_outcome: A replaceable, provenance-friendly geomorphology layer that produces stable surface deformation independent from SurfaceCellKey, LOD, camera and representation and can later feed geology/volume/detail stages.
G.progress_note: G8.5 Cross-Cell / Cross-LOD Geomorphology Invariance remains ACCEPTED on exact-Windows tested head 6cc0c2b5ff1bc21a5b488a8492ef8cce28fa4736. G8.6 first exact-Windows run on 87acbc69854336fa52b5b4c66069ec56a555c1a4 passed editor import and G8.5 parent invariance (150 assertions), then stopped in the G8.6 contract harness at 35 assertions / 1 failure: source grid pinned. The manifest remains correct at 33x17. Root cause is acceptance-harness-only: JSON.parse_string decodes numeric array elements as float and GDScript Array equality is type-sensitive, so [33.0,17.0] != [33,17]. This behavior was independently reproduced on exact a13da4feb Linux double. FIX1 at 05757e69b7e73139226c68702f4bb81c31840469 changes only the harness to validate source_grid length and cast both values to int. No lab runtime, geomorphology formula, canonical truth, identity or presentation behavior changed. Focused FIX1 retest, automated world/core regression and manual graphical acceptance remain required.
G.next_stage: Sync latest feature/g8-geomorphology and rerun RUN_G8_6_GEOMORPHOLOGY_VISUAL_LAB_TESTS.ps1. If green, keep the exact clean checkout and run RUN_G8_6_AUTOMATED_ACCEPTANCE.ps1 without fetch/reset. Then launch the G8.6 scene and complete the manual graphical checks. DOCTRINE.short_description: Design doctrine describing how a large simulated world produces discovery, capability, infrastructure, consequences and history.
DOCTRINE.purpose: Keep gameplay/world-building principles reusable and aligned with technical foundations without giving design documentation ownership of identity, authority, material or persistence systems.
DOCTRINE.expected_outcome: A durable design reference used to judge whether new simulation mechanics create interesting interconnected gameplay rather than isolated features.
DOCTRINE.progress_note: Doctrine remains an active design reference and must map new mechanics onto canonical queries, operations, transactions and persistent world consequences.
DOCTRINE.next_stage: Continue doctrine updates only when new gameplay/system evidence appears
